title: Progressive Empty-State Modules + In-Product Learning Strip for Console
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary: Design a lightweight, composable set of empty-state modules (Progressive Empty-State Modules, PEMs) and an adjacent, dismissible Learning Strip that surfaces context-sensitive micro-guides, templates, and first-run actions across the Redwood Console. Focus areas: Dashboards (cost & latency cards), Rollouts page (canary/A-B flows), and Cost views. Goal is to increase activation (first successful deployment or first cost-optimization action) while keeping the Console uncluttered for experienced users.

Why now: New onboarding metrics show users drop off on empty dashboard and rollouts pages. Current one-off tours are noisy and hard to maintain per page. PEM + Learning Strip provides reusable building blocks, easier A/B testing per module, and targeted education near the primary CTA.

Scope:
- Design 3 PEM variants: Quick-start (single CTA), Guided checklist (multi-step inline items), Template carousel (prebuilt config snippets).
- Learning Strip: narrow, right-anchored panel that shows 1–2 contextual tips, a single-action template, and a link to the knowledge center. Collapsible/dismissible per user with persistent opt-out in local storage and telemetry.
- Target pages: Dashboards (empty cost/latency cards), Rollouts (no active rollouts), Cost views (no cost data / trial accounts).
- Accessibility: keyboard focus-trap when strip opens, screen reader labels for tip items, contrast and motion-reduced variants.

Out of scope for this ticket: backend analytics pipelines, billing integration, and extensive localization (we will design with strings-ready tokens and provide sample translations).

Deliverables:
- Figma spec + clickable prototype (desktop + responsive)
- Component inventory and tokens for engineering handoff
- Acceptance criteria and A/B test plan
- Annotated accessibility checklist

Non-goals / constraints: Keep initial surface small (max 1 PEM per page), avoid persistent banners that increase cognitive load, no mandatory modal-based tours in v1.
acceptance_criteria: PEM components exist in Figma with 3 variants and documented states (empty, loading, dismissed)
Learning Strip prototype demonstrates show/hide, collapse, dismiss, and persistent opt-out flows
Design tokens and spacing grid for PEMs provided in the handoff doc
Telemetry events enumerated for tip_shown, tip_clicked, template_applied, tip_dismissed
A/B test plan defined with primary metric: first-deployment-or-cost-action within 7 days (activation), and secondary metrics: tip CTR and dismiss rate
Accessibility checklist completed: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, reduced-motion variant
